name: Exact finite sample-to-scaled-Taylor interpolation noise amplification law

statement.note_ascii: for distinct finite sample nodes, exact rational Vandermonde interpolation followed by a declared diagonal Taylor-row scaling has the displayed induced infinity norm; any separately certified sample-space measurement and truncation radii are amplified by the same finite operator

definitions.V: power Vandermonde matrix V[j,n]=t_j^n for distinct sample nodes
definitions.D_h: diag(1,h,...,h^(m-1)) for nonzero sample spacing h
definitions.S: declared diagonal scaling of recovered Taylor/interpolation coefficients
definitions.r_sample: separately certified sample-space model/Taylor remainder radius

parents.evidence: PROP-EPSC-37 supplies a derivative-free finite sample chart structurally; PROP-EPSC-38 quantifies the distinct sample-to-scaled-Taylor intermediate reconstruction operator
narrows the open measurement interface by identifying and exactly quantifying one potentially ill-conditioned intermediate route

claim_boundary: Finite interpolation linear algebra only. It does not certify the conditioning of the direct nonlinear sample map, an ODE/PDE flow remainder, physical sensor noise, branch capture, arbitrary finite N, continuum completion, Navier-Stokes regularity, or the Clay Millennium problem. In the current fixed-N=1 application, the severe small-h amplification applies to reconstruction of the existing scaled Taylor chart and is not a no-go theorem for direct finite-time sample inversion.
